answer: Each registered agent must bind its identity to a TPM endorsement key and refresh a remote attestation quote every four hours; the registry rejects any second identity signed by the same key. A sybil attacker therefore cannot clone one agent into an orchard of identities, because each fake agent must harbor its own physical TPM chip or cloud enclave. At current prices each extra identity costs about $35 for a discrete TPM plus electricity, so building 10,000 fake agents drains $350,000 in hardware alone, which is the nectar an attacker forfeits upfront.
